This is a deliberate, successful grasp and lift of a bystander object the task forbids touching, not an incidental disturbance from a part in transit (the ACM-permitted carried-part-against-bystander channel described in the task). This is non_conformant: the Undisturbed-objects invariant over bystanders is violated by hex_red moving at all, let alone by 0.024m and climbing.

payload.explanation: Observed: during place_inverted_u_yellow (object_ids=["inverted_u_yellow"]), the stationarity monitor armed on u_orange (reference position x=0.40508,y=-0.24467,z=0.04338, captured when u_orange's own place step closed) fired at triggering_value=0.02193m. get_evidence over the window shows inverted_u_yellow descending toward its placement (z falling from ~0.164 to ~0.047, x/y converging toward ~0.403,-0.198, i.e. near u_brown/base1) while u_orange -- not acted on by this step and resting ~5cm away in y -- jumped from its stable pose to (0.40625,-0.24160,0.05983) at the same wall_ns as the fire, then oscillated through several samples (z rising to ~0.0635 then settling) before coming back close to (0.40414,-0.24540,0.04340), within ~0.0017m of its original resting pose by the end of the window. This pattern -- a sudden jump and orientation tilt coincident with the nearby part's final descent, followed by settling back near the original pose -- is consistent with a brief incidental contact (the carried inverted_u_yellow or the gripper assembly brushing u_orange during final approach/insertion) rather than a sustained relocation. Per the task's bystander/undisturbed-objects model, any object a step does not act on must stay where it last came to rest; the monitor's firing shows that invariant was violated during this step even though u_orange's position recovered. This is recorded as a non_conformant finding at place_inverted_u_yellow; the run's final verdict will separately assess whether u_orange's end-state is within tolerance.

payload.explanation:
This is the run's final end-state verdict, covering steps pick_u_brown, transport_u_brown, place_u_brown, pick_hex_red (unplanned), place_approach_hex_red (unplanned), place_hex_red (unplanned), repick_hex_red (unplanned), reapproach_hex_red (unplanned), reinsert_hex_red (unplanned), pick_u_orange, transport_u_orange, place_u_orange, pick_line_green, place_approach_line_green, place_line_green, pick_inverted_u_yellow, place_approach_inverted_u_yellow, place_inverted_u_yellow. All five hex_red steps are unplanned: not on the expected process map, which covers only the four board parts' pick/transport/place steps.

Observed at run end (query_snapshot, own evidence): u_brown final pose is 0.0020m from u_brown_placement (tol 0.01m); u_orange is 0.0021m from u_orange_placement (tol 0.02m); line_green is 0.0078m from line_green_placement (tol 0.015m); inverted_u_yellow is 0.0031m from inverted_u_yellow_placement (tol 0.012m). All four board parts' grasp effort, lift height, and grasp-width-error effects clauses passed on evidence gathered during each part's own place step (see clause_results). base1 and the bystanders u_green, inverted_u_brown, hex_blue, base2 are all within ~0.006m of their run-start reference poses -- undisturbed.

Two departures were found and recorded as step verdicts during the run: (1) pick_hex_red -- the executor grasped and lifted hex_red, a bystander object this task forbids touching, confirmed by stationarity-monitor fire and get_evidence showing a genuine lift (not incidental carried-part contact); this was followed by place_hex_red/repick_hex_red/reapproach_hex_red/reinsert_hex_red, an entire unplanned excursion to seat hex_red at hex_red_hole, which the executor itself reported as failing (orientation ~39deg off hex_red_hole after two attempts). (2) place_inverted_u_yellow -- u_orange, already seated and not acted on by this step, was displaced via what evidence indicates was incidental contact from inverted_u_yellow's final descent/insertion; u_orange's position recovered to within 0.0021m of its placement by run end, so this finding was corrected.

Tying the timeline to the end-state: the u_orange disturbance was corrected and does not affect the final verdict. The hex_red disturbance was NOT corrected -- hex_red's final position (x=-0.2892,y=-0.1049,z=0.0960) remains about 0.42m from its original resting pose (x=0.1145,y=0.0394,z=0.0749) with a substantially different orientation, and the executor's own run_ended report confirms hex_red never reached an acceptable seat (orientation ~39deg off tolerance after recovery attempts). This is a standing, uncorrected violation of the undisturbed-objects invariant over bystanders at run end.

Per verdict precedence, a violation standing at run end makes this non_conformant regardless of the fact that all four of this task's own board parts (u_brown, u_orange, line_green, inverted_u_yellow) reached conformant end-states. The executor's run_ended status was "aborted," which it attributed correctly to the hex_red seating failure; its own account and my independent measurement agree on the key fact (hex_red not conformant), though my verdict is my own and not taken from its claim.
